edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: The proposed pathway combines changes in oxidative damage, inflammatory tone, hormone signaling, bile-acid metabolism, and exposure to food-derived carcinogens or protective phytochemicals. For Breast cancer, those pathways matter over years, so consistent long-term intake patterns are more informative than short interventions.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link extra-virgin olive oil to lower risk of breast cancer in adult women. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
